stories.title: Air India flight delayed seven hours after hoax hijack note
stories.summary: Air India flight AI2772 from Kolkata to Mumbai was delayed seven hours on Wednesday after a handwritten hijack threat was found in a lavatory. Police detained a passenger who reportedly claimed he wrote the note to avoid a work trip. The threat was declared a hoax by authorities.

stories.title: Hijack note delays Air India flight to Mumbai by hours
stories.summary: A hijack threat note found on a Mumbai-bound Air India flight from Kolkata led to significant delays and a full security protocol before being declared a hoax. Key Points - A Mumbai-bound Air India flight from Kolkata faced a hijack threat before take-off on Wednesday

stories.title: Akasa Air quarterly losses widen by 57 percent
stories.summary: Akasa Air reported a net loss of approximately 550 crore rupees for the first quarter of FY27, up from 350 crore rupees in the same period last year. The airline cited high fuel costs and foreign exchange fluctuations. It maintains it remains well capitalised and focused on growth.

stories.title: Mangaluru airport begins terminal expansion
stories.summary: Mangaluru International Airport has broken ground on an integrated terminal expansion project. The airport aims to increase its annual passenger capacity from 2.5 million to 5.2 million over the next three years. The project intends to introduce new technologies to improve passenger convenience and operational efficiency for airlines.

stories.title: IndiGo cancels flights at Ahmedabad airport
stories.summary: IndiGo cancelled flights to Nashik and Bhopal at Ahmedabad Airport on Thursday, leaving passengers stranded. Some travellers were notified only an hour before departure after completing boarding and luggage check-in. The cancellations resulted in protests inside the terminal as passengers confronted staff over the lack of alternative arrangements.

stories.title: Air India Flight AI 2772 From Kolkata To Mumbai Delayed After Suspected Hijack Threat Note Found In Lavatory, 108 On Boa
stories.summary: Mumbai: Air India's scheduled flight AI-2772, operating on the Mumbai-Kolkata sectore, was scheduled to take-off at 10.20am. However, a cabin crew member discovered a handwritten threat note inside the lavatory of the aircraft to registered as VT-TNH to about 45 mins before the scheduled departure

stories.title: Mumbai airport to maintain international traffic during terminal rebuild
stories.summary: Around 91 percent of international traffic at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport will remain unaffected during the redevelopment of Terminal 1. Most international carriers will continue operations from Terminal 2. About 9 percent of the airport's annual passenger volume is expected to shift to Navi Mumbai International Airport.

stories.title: Air India losses narrow in first half of fiscal year
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines reported its share of losses from Air India fell to 2,720 crore rupees in the first half of FY2026-27, down from 3,229 crore rupees a year earlier. The figures suggest total losses for the Tata-owned airline dropped to approximately 10,837 crore rupees during the period.

stories.title: Hijack threat to Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight turns out to be hoax, aircraft takes off after seven-hour delay
stories.summary: A hijack threat to a Mumbai-bound Air India flight at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport in Kolkata turned out to be a hoax on Wednesday, with the aircraft departing for its destination at 5.38 pm after security checks. The flight, AI 2772, was

stories.title: Singapore Airlines reports progress in Air India transformation
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines stated that Air India is making tangible progress in its multi-year transformation. The group reported a net profit of 134 million Singapore dollars for the six months ending September 2026, noting that the result was aided by a lower share of losses from its Indian associate.

stories.summary: Hijack threat note found in Air India flight lavatory, 105 passengers deboarded A hijack threat note found on a Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight on Wednesday prompted security officials to move the aircraft to an isolation bay. 105 passengers were deboarded while agencies carried out security

stories.title: JetBlue introduces first-class seating
stories.summary: JetBlue has unveiled BlueFirst, a new first-class seating option, as it attempts to return to profitability. The airline has spent years losing money and hopes the premium seats will help offset high fuel costs. The new chairs resemble standard domestic first-class seating found on other major carriers.

stories.title: The Boeing 737 NG Still Has Years Of Flying Left, But Its Largest Operator Doesn't Want It Anymore
stories.summary: The symbiotic relationship between Southwest Airlines and the Boeing 737 Next Generation family has defined the very essence of low-cost domestic travel. Operating hundreds of Boeing 737-700 and Boeing 737-800 aircraft, the carrier built its legendary point-to-point network around the reliability, commonality, and rugged versatility

stories.title: Alaska Airlines to launch service in Des Moines
stories.summary: Alaska Airlines will begin service at Des Moines International Airport in June 2027. The carrier will initially operate one daily nonstop flight to its Seattle hub. This marks the first new airline to serve the airport since 2012. The full details are available for subscribers.

stories.title: Breeze Airways reports four profitable quarters
stories.summary: Breeze Airways founder David Neeleman said the airline has recorded four consecutive profitable quarters. The privately held carrier aims to avoid direct competition with major airlines to maintain its margins. Neeleman credited the airline's profitability to creating its own demand rather than chasing traditional industry metrics.

stories.title: Alaska Airlines to launch Jacksonville service
stories.summary: Alaska Airlines will begin nonstop flights between Jacksonville and Seattle in June 2027. The daily service will use a Boeing 737, making Jacksonville International Airport a host to all 11 major U.S. airlines. The airport has been waiting for one final logo to complete its collection.

stories.title: Air Canada trims network with ten route cancellations
stories.summary: Air Canada has cancelled ten routes that operated during the summer, including eight international and two domestic services. The airline currently holds 37 percent of the international market and 30 percent of domestic flights. Route churn remains a standard feature of the network.

stories.title: Air Canada operations chief calls for better reliability
stories.summary: Air Canada executive Mark Nasr says the carrier is the original premium airline in North America, citing early investments in lie-flat seats. However, Nasr admits the airline needs to improve its on-time performance to be fully premium. The airline is currently working on arriving when it says it will.

stories.title: Magnifica Air revealed as buyer of 10 Airbus corporate jets
stories.summary: Magnifica Air has been identified as the buyer of 10 Airbus ACJ220-300 aircraft. The Florida-based airline plans to launch in 2028 with a 17-jet fleet, offering 54-seat cabins that combine private aviation services with scheduled flights. The airline intends to provide concierge assistance to its passengers.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific A330neo Order Grows to 41 | MiGFlug
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific has not taken delivery of a single Airbus A330neo yet. On Wednesday 11 November, it ordered eleven more anyway. Airbus announced from Toulouse that Hong Kong’s Cathay Group had placed a firm order for 14 additional aircraft: eleven A330-900s and three single-aisle A321neos.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific orders 14 additional Airbus jets
stories.summary: Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 11 A330-900 widebodies and three A321neo narrowbody aircraft in a deal valued at 5.1 billion dollars. The order brings the group's total commitment for the A330-900 to 41 jets. The aircraft are intended to support regional growth and fleet renewal.

stories.summary: HONG KONG- Cathay Pacific (CX) is expanding its aircraft fleet with an additional order for 11 Airbus A330-900 widebody aircraft, valued at approximately US$5.1 billion. Announced on November 11, 2026, the purchase will strengthen the airline’s regional operations, increase passenger and cargo capacity, and support

stories.title: FAA halts flights at LaGuardia and Newark
stories.summary: Heavy rain and thunderstorms have triggered ground stops at LaGuardia and John F. Kennedy International airports, with significant delays reported at Newark. The FAA reports some flight restrictions are causing delays averaging more than two hours. Passengers are advised to check directly with their airlines for updates.

stories.title: FAA awards Deloitte $488 million modernization contract
stories.summary: The FAA awarded Deloitte Consulting a contract with a ceiling of $488.2 million to modernize legacy applications and systems. The ATLAS program targets a portfolio of approximately 200 applications and 3,000 databases. The contract could run for up to 10 years if all options are exercised.

stories.title: FAA grants first high-seas drone waiver to Skyways
stories.summary: The FAA authorized Skyways to fly its hybrid-electric V2 drone beyond visual line of sight from the Louisiana coast to a Shell platform in the Gulf of Mexico. The waiver allows drone operations without rulemaking. The drone will conduct pipeline inspections and a mock equipment delivery.

stories.title: FAA Expands AI-Assisted Traffic Management Nationwide
stories.summary: The FAA is expanding its artificial intelligence-supported air traffic management system to all 22 air route traffic control centers nationwide. According to a Nov. 10 statement, the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system will be used to help reduce delays and fuel

stories.title: Federal watchdog to audit helicopter tourism oversight
stories.summary: The Department of Transportation’s Office of Inspector General will audit the FAA’s oversight of helicopter tourism. The review follows congressional pressure regarding safety and noise concerns. Auditors will examine whether some operators classify flights as aerial photography to avoid stricter safety rules. The audit is pending.

stories.title: FAA orders inspections on 2,000 Boeing 737 jets
stories.summary: The FAA issued a directive requiring inspections on 1,987 U.S.-registered Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft. Carriers reported mid-flight pitch oscillations caused by mechanical wear and excessive looseness in hinges and jackscrews. The mandate takes effect November 23, 2026, and excludes the newer 737 MAX models.

stories.title: FAA expands AI traffic tool nationwide
stories.summary: The FAA is expanding its AI-assisted traffic planning tool, SMART, to all 22 U.S. air route traffic control centers. The agency says the system, which uses 200 data streams, helped reroute 180 flights in the Washington area, saving an average of 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel.

stories.title: FAA Expands SMART Traffic Planning to All 22 Centers
stories.summary: WASHINGTON , The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is expanding its Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system to airspace managed by all 22 FAA centers, extending a traffic-planning tool first used in the Washington region in September. The agency’s November 10 expansion statement

stories.title: Training aircraft hard-lands at Solapur airport
stories.summary: A Tecnam P-Mentor training aircraft operated by Redbird Flying Training Academy hard-landed at Solapur airport, damaging its nose wheel. The trainee pilot was uninjured. Sources indicated the pilot was practicing landings when the aircraft came down hard. The aircraft remained stranded on the runway.

stories.title: ATP Flight School opens Dayton training center
stories.summary: ATP Flight School is opening a training facility at Dayton International Airport, bringing its network to 87 locations. The company says its program allows students with zero flight experience to earn commercial certifications in nine months. Students then transition into structured, airline-backed career tracks.

stories.title: Epic Flight Academy opens Connecticut location
stories.summary: Epic Flight Academy has opened its 12th FAA Part 141 flight school at Danbury Municipal Airport. The facility held a ribbon-cutting ceremony on October 17, 2026, where visitors toured the school and used the flight simulator. The school operates under FAA Part 141 certification.

stories.title: Luke Air Force Base transitions to F-35 training
stories.summary: The 56th Fighter Wing is shifting to exclusively F-35A Lightning II training for U.S. pilots at Luke Air Force Base. The transition ends nearly five decades of F-16 training at the site. The base is remodeling infrastructure and installing new simulators to support the F-35 program.

stories.title: Oklahoma State to open aviation school
stories.summary: Oklahoma State University will open a School of Aviation and Space in July 2027. University leaders say the move will help meet workforce demands and support the state’s aerospace industry, which generates over $52 billion in annual economic activity. The school will expand existing aviation program offerings.

stories.title: Air Force nears completion of pilot training revamp
stories.summary: The 19th Air Force is finishing a five-year project to shift from time-based pilot training to a competency-based curriculum. The new approach uses data from past courses to map required skills for specific airframes. Previously, readiness was measured primarily by flight hours and simulator time.

stories.title: AZAL training center plans to expand pilot training capacity in Gabala
stories.summary: The Azerbaijan Airlines Flight Crew Training Center in Gabala plans to expand its capacity to train local pilots. The center currently operates five Cessna 172S aircraft and expects to increase that number to more than 10 by 2028. The center is prioritizing local personnel for its training programs.

stories.title: Hillsboro Aero Academy hosts Milan recruitment event for European pilots
stories.summary: US-based Hillsboro Aero Academy is holding an information seminar in Milan on November 22 to recruit European students for its flight training programs. The event aims to introduce prospective pilots to FAA and EASA training pathways and US student visa options. The academy is looking for students abroad.

stories.title: EgyptAir Training Academy renews EASA simulator approval
stories.summary: The EgyptAir Training Academy has renewed its European Union Aviation Safety Agency approval for the operation and maintenance of its flight simulation training devices. The renewal follows a regulatory inspection in Cairo and allows the academy to continue providing EASA-qualified simulator training to its airline customers.

stories.title: Regiment 915 focuses on helicopter pilot training quality
stories.summary: The 915th Regiment has identified the improvement of helicopter pilot training as a central political task. The program emphasizes a combination of theoretical knowledge, practical skills and psychological fortitude. Trainees are expected to develop critical thinking and the demeanor of a military pilot through their flight training sessions.

stories.title: K-State Salina gains FAA self-examining authority for instrument ratings
stories.summary: Kansas State University Salina has received FAA approval to grant instrument ratings without using outside examiners. Students can now complete testing through university instructors, a change officials say eliminates wait times and saves students up to $1,000 in fees. The university already holds similar authority for primary ratings.

stories.title: Indian Air Force may extend HAL Kiran service life to 2030
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force is considering extending the life of its HAL Kiran jet trainers to 2030, past the original 2027 retirement date. The extension follows delays in procuring replacements and the aircraft's new role as a testbed for unmanned systems. The fleet first flew in 1964.
